Detailed Rubric
Use this rubric to self-assess your work before submission. The "Common Mistakes" column reflects typical deductions — review each point carefully.
Task
Marks
Type
Key Requirements
Common Mistakes to Avoid
Task 1: Data Acquisition & Loading
Group
Datasets sourced from approved platforms (Kaggle, Tableau Public, data.gov.au, abs.gov.au, GitHub, Quandl)
Join or Union applied — at least two datasets combined
Reasons for dataset selection clearly stated
Problem-solving potential described (what questions can be answered?)
Direct links to all source datasets included in the report
Using a single CSV file (violates Join/Union requirement)
No justification for why these datasets were chosen
Missing source dataset links
Datasets not from approved sources
Task 2A: Data Exploration & Cleaning
Group
Data dictionary includes: row count, column count, data types, formats, file sizes, keywords, descriptions, and example values
Top 10-15 attributes documented if dataset has >30 fields
Descriptive statistics for numeric fields: distinct count, null %, sum, min, max, mean, median, mode, std dev
Descriptive statistics for categorical fields: distinct count, null %
Missing value handling strategy clearly described
Outlier detection and treatment discussed
Data dictionary missing data types, formats, or example values
Descriptive statistics are generic and not tied to the specific dataset
No discussion of outliers
Missing value strategy not explained
All >30 fields documented without prioritising relevant ones
Task 2B: Data Transformation
Group
All transformation steps are described in the report (not just listed)
Steps include: filter, rename columns, change data types, remove rows/columns, split values, replace nulls, remove duplicates
Explanation of what was changed and why it was necessary
Before/after comparison or effect on data described where relevant
Only listing transformation steps without explaining what or why
No before/after context — unclear what changed
Missing categories of transformation (e.g., no null handling discussed)
Transformations not shown to be applied in the BI tool
Task 3A: Visualisations
Group
At least FOUR different visualisation types used
Each chart type is different (no repetition)
Justification for each chart type: data nature, relationships highlighted, and audience considered
BI tool name included in each figure caption
Using the same chart type more than once (e.g., four bar charts)
No justification provided for chart type choices
BI tool name missing from figure captions
Fewer than four visualisation types
Task 3B: Static Dashboard
Group
Dashboard includes titles, captions, and legends
Single vs. multi-screen decision explicitly explained and justified
Layout arrangement rationale explained (why visualisations are in this order/position)
Dashboard is visually coherent and aesthetically designed
Published dashboard link included if screenshots are unclear
No explanation of single vs. multi-screen decision
Missing titles, captions, or legends on visualisations
No rationale for the layout arrangement
Dashboard link missing when screenshots are low quality
.twbx file submitted (not accepted)
Task 4: Interpretation
Group
Target audience is explicitly identified
Insights address the target audience's specific needs and questions
Impact on decision-making is highlighted
Findings connected to real-world scenarios or business contexts
At least one actionable recommendation provided
Interpretation only describes what the chart shows — no "so what"
No actionable recommendations
Audience not defined or too vague ("everyone")
No connection to real-world decision-making
Task 5: Contribution / Reflection
Individual
All five prompts addressed: (1) Contribution & Responsibilities, (2) Collaboration & Teamwork, (3) Learning & Growth, (4) Challenges & Lessons Learned, (5) Use of Generative AI
Reflection is specific and personalised — not generic
AI usage clearly disclosed (tools used, purpose, limitations)
Written in first person with concrete examples
Generic reflection that could apply to any project or any person
Missing one or more of the five prompt areas
No disclosure of generative AI use (or non-use)
Copied from another member's reflection
Presentation (Group)
Group
Covers Tasks 1 through 4 in the presentation
All group members actively participate and present
Slides are visually appealing and professionally designed
Smooth coordination between members; no awkward handoffs
Q&A handled correctly and confidently (8 marks)
Logical flow from introduction to conclusion (2 marks)
Going over the time limit
Not covering all four tasks in the slides
One member dominating the presentation while others do not speak
Slides are text-heavy with no visuals
Unable to answer basic Q&A questions about the data or analysis
Presentation (Individual)
Individual
Presents their assigned section correctly and clearly (3 marks)
Present and participating on the presentation day (1 mark)
Speaks for at least 2 minutes during the presentation (1 mark)
Absent on presentation day (forfeits all 5 individual marks)
Speaking for less than 2 minutes
Reading directly from slides without explanation
Presenting incorrectly or confusing the data
General Notes
Word limit: 2,000 words ±10% (body text only). Do not count the title page, references, or appendices.
Name your BI tool (e.g., Tableau) at the start of each task section AND in every figure caption.
Turnitin similarity score must be below 20%. Submit with enough time to revise if needed.
Submission filenames: G[GroupNumber]Assg5-Report.docx and G[GroupNumber]Assg5-Slides.pptx
Do NOT submit .twbx files. Use screenshots plus a Tableau Public link.
Each group member must present for at least 2 minutes in person during Week 11 or 12.
